newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Pertamina says oil rig catches fire.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Pertamina says oil rig catches fire.

text.p: Indonesian state oil company Pertamina said on Tuesday that an offshore oil rig near the town of Balikpapan in East Kalimantan province caught fire on Sunday after gas bubbled to the surface.
It said the fire was under control and there were no casualties.
The Attaka oil field and the offshore Santan field were shut down as a precautionary measure, it said.
Pertamina said in a statement that gas began bubbling to the surface early on Sunday at the Attaka Echo Platform and that all personnel were evacuated from the oil rig.
It said the platform caught fire at 5:20 p.m. (0920 GMT) on Sunday and later sank into the sea. However, a gas fire continued to burn over the sea, it said.
Later that evening both the Attaka and nearby Santan fields were shut down, the statement said.
If there was no oil discharge and the gas fire diminished, the fields would be restarted, it said.
The Jakarta Post newspaper estimated losees from the fire at between 18 billion rupiah and 42 billion rupiah.
The oil rig is owned by Unocal Indonesia Co, a unit of Unocal Corp .
